prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1063; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a side impact at an intersection. The insured reports the other vehicle entered on a red signal and struck the driver's side door.

Entry 2: Police report obtained. The responding officer confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision and notes the scene layout matches the account given.

Entry 3: Spoke with the insured, who confirmed that the driver is named on the policy and that the vehicle was insured on the date of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 4: Claimant is represented by counsel. All further contact to go through the attorney's office. Requested medical authorizations and prior records.

Entry 5: Recorded statement taken from the claimant's representative. The claimant has described the collision the same way in every conversation so far, including the sequence of impact and the position of the vehicles.

Entry 6: Witness statements and scene photographs reviewed. Witnesses, the photos and the other driver all agree the accident happened as described.

Entry 7: Field inspection completed. Damage is consistent with a side impact to the driver's door and panel. A few old scratches near the rear wheel well may be older than this crash, so they are noted separately for now.

Entry 8: Medical records received showing neck and back strain. It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash, and the treating notes do not yet address the question directly.

Entry 9: Treatment has run somewhat longer than usual for this type of strain. No earlier injury to the same body area is known from the records requested so far. Follow-up with the treating physician is pending.

Entry 10: Repair estimate reviewed. It is not clear whether all of the listed damage came from this impact, so the body shop has been asked to separate pre-existing wear from new collision damage.

Entry 11: File remains open pending medical causation review, the repair breakdown, and a response from the claimant's attorney on the outstanding records request.
